blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, the general ledger is the long memory of the institution. Every decision, every transaction, every correction ever made lives somewhere in its history. A company that keeps its ledger clean and explainable can answer almost any question about its past — from 'how did we account for that acquisition in 2019?' to 'why did this account balance jump in March three years ago?'

A company that has let its ledger drift — with codes that nobody remembers creating, balances that nobody can explain, and entries posted to 'miscellaneous' because nobody had the time — gradually loses access to its own history. When questions finally come, from auditors, regulators, or a new CFO trying to understand the business, the answers take weeks instead of minutes.

The senior finance leader's quiet job is to protect the ledger across years, knowing that the real value of a clean ledger only appears when something difficult happens and the answer is already there, waiting to be read.

items.q: According to the text, what is the general ledger at senior level?
options: A summary of the current quarter
The long memory of the institution
A tool used only during audits
items.why: "the general ledger is the long memory of the institution" — é a tese de abertura do texto.

items.q: What happens when a company lets its ledger drift?
options: It closes its books faster each month
It gradually loses access to its own history
items.why: "gradually loses access to its own history" — códigos e saldos ninguém mais explica.

items.q: The text implies that entries posted to 'miscellaneous' were made because…
options: the amounts were too small to classify
nobody had the time to classify them properly
items.why: Inferência: "posted to 'miscellaneous' because nobody had the time" — atalho por falta de tempo, não decisão técnica.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A drifted ledger makes questions slower to answer.
The value of a tidy ledger is visible in routine months, not hard ones.
Protecting the ledger is a long-term responsibility.
A clean ledger proves its worth mainly in difficult moments.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o valor real "only appears when something difficult happens" — o contrário da opção escolhida.

items.q: What does the contrast 'weeks instead of minutes' most strongly suggest?
options: Ledgers should be archived after three years
New CFOs are inefficient by nature
Neglect has a delayed but real cost that surfaces under pressure
items.why: Inferência: o descuido não cobra na hora, mas cobra caro quando a pergunta difícil chega.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily localizando a resposta no razão. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Give me two minutes — I think I can find it. The question is about a payment we made four years ago, and the new director wants to know why it was split across two accounts.

Right, here it is. See the reference? Whoever posted this didn't just book the number; they left a note, they cross-referenced the contract, and they used the proper code instead of dumping it into miscellaneous. So I can tell you exactly what happened, and I can tell you who approved it.

Honestly, this is the whole point. Nobody thanks you for a clean ledger in a quiet month. But the day a regulator or an auditor walks in with a question about something from years ago, the answer is either already sitting there, waiting to be read — or it isn't, and then you're paying three analysts to reconstruct history from bank statements.

We've protected this ledger entry by entry since I joined. It looks like housekeeping. It isn't. It's the reason I can answer a four-year-old question before the coffee's even cold.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What question is the new director asking Emily?
options: Why a payment from four years ago was split across two accounts
Whether the ledger should be replaced
How much the company spent last quarter
Which auditor signed off on the accounts
items.why: "a payment we made four years ago… why it was split across two accounts."

items.q: Why is Emily able to explain exactly what happened?
options: She was personally involved in the original transaction
The entry included a note, a cross-reference and the proper code
She reconstructed it from bank statements
items.why: "they left a note, they cross-referenced the contract, and they used the proper code."

items.q: What does Emily mean by 'Nobody thanks you for a clean ledger in a quiet month'?
options: The value of the discipline is invisible until a hard question arrives
items.why: Inferência: o esforço só é reconhecido quando o problema difícil aparece — não no dia a dia.

items.q: What is the implied cost of NOT protecting the ledger, according to Emily?
options: Paying analysts to reconstruct history from bank statements
Failing to close the month on time
Losing access to the banking system
items.why: Inferência: a alternativa ao registro limpo é "paying three analysts to reconstruct history from bank statements."

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's attitude toward the ledger work?
options: She is indifferent to how entries are posted
She quietly takes pride in it and defends its real value
She thinks it should be outsourced
She sees it as tedious housekeeping with little payoff
items.why: Inferência: "It looks like housekeeping. It isn't." — ela reconhece e valoriza o trabalho.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A ledger is only useful if every balance is explainable." Explainable means…
options: able to be justified and accounted for
items.why: Explainable = explicável: cada saldo pode ser justificado, sua origem pode ser rastreada.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The 2019 ___ added three subsidiaries whose books we still have to consolidate."
items.why: Acquisition = aquisição: a compra de outra empresa, que trouxe as subsidiárias.

items.q: "Over the years the coding standards were allowed to drift." To drift here means to…
options: move away gradually from what was intended
items.why: To drift = desviar: afastar-se aos poucos do padrão, sem que ninguém decida isso conscientemente.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Anything we couldn't classify quickly ended up in ___ , and now nobody can explain it."
items.why: Miscellaneous = diversos: a conta "tapa-buraco" onde se joga o que não se teve tempo de classificar.

items.q: Institutional memory is best described as…
options: the tenure of the finance team
what the organisation retains about why things were done
items.why: É o conhecimento acumulado sobre as razões das decisões — o que um razão limpo preserva.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas de finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the year-end adjustments." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Before we close the books, let's reconcile the two accounts." To reconcile means to…
options: make two sets of figures agree
items.why: Reconcile = reconciliar: conferir e fazer bater dois conjuntos de números.

items.q: "When the audit comes, that sloppy entry will come back to haunt us." This means it will…
options: cause problems later because of past neglect
items.why: Come back to haunt = voltar para assombrar: um erro antigo que cobra a conta depois.

items.q: "We can't just write off the discrepancy without an explanation." To write off here means to…
options: remove an amount from the books as a loss
items.why: Write off = dar baixa / lançar como perda, retirando o valor dos livros.

items.q: "A clean ledger only pays off when a hard question arrives." To pay off means to…
options: produce a worthwhile result after effort
items.why: Pay off = compensar, dar retorno: o esforço acumulado rende no momento decisivo.
